explanation: From the 1920s, American stop signs were yellow octagons; the United States switched them to red in 1954. Japan uses a red downward-pointing triangle.

claims.text: In most countries the stop sign is an octagon.
Give way, no entry and speed limit signs are not octagonal.
From the 1920s, standard stop signs in the United States were yellow octagons (the first, in Detroit in 1915, was a white square).
The United States changed its stop signs to red with white letters in 1954.
Japan's stop sign is a red downward-pointing triangle.

evidence.restatement: Give way signs are downward-pointing triangles, no entry signs are round (red with a white bar), and speed limit signs are round or, in North America, upright rectangles. None is an octagon.
